lines.text: Why write the same block a hundred times? Loops let computers repeat — that’s where their power comes from.
A counted loop (repeat 4) runs the blocks inside it exactly 4 times.
To draw a regular polygon, the turns must add up to 360 degrees.
So each turn is 360 ÷ number of sides.
Store the number of sides in a variable and use an operator for the turn.
Change one number to get any polygon.
Programmers say DRY: Don’t Repeat Yourself.
Loops make code shorter, clearer and easier to change.
Here is the same loop in Python. “for i in range(sides)” repeats the indented lines, just like the repeat block.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
